reading: A to the positive integer power k equals P times D to that power times P inverse. A is diagonalizable using the eigenvector basis P; diagonal entries of D are raised to power k.

reading: A equals U times capital Sigma times V transpose. For real m-by-n A, U and V are square orthogonal matrices of sizes m and n; Sigma is m by n with nonnegative diagonal singular values. Sigma is a matrix name here, not a summation sign.

reading: X transpose A transpose A x equals the squared Euclidean norm of Ax, which is nonnegative. Here A is a real matrix and x is any compatible real column. This establishes that A transpose A is positive semidefinite.
